Outcomes

Show exactly what you built.

The programme is designed around eight working projects, an individual skills record and 16–20 weeks of engineering work. Graduate and placement data will follow as cohorts complete the programme.

What graduates can show

Eight working projects

A portfolio with designs, code and videos lets an employer review the work before an interview.

An Engineering Passport

A record of the practical tests you passed shows exactly which skills you demonstrated on your own.

A semester of engineering work

Work full time for 16–20 weeks in a company or in the Product Studio, contributing to a team on practical problems.

A four-year B.Tech pathway

Ask admissions for the awarding university, approved degree title and campus details for the course you are considering.

Where each course can lead

Electronics and Computer Engineering

Embedded systems, firmware, edge AI, connected products and EV electronics.

VLSI Design and Technology

Chip design, verification and physical design.

Robotics and Artificial Intelligence

Robotics, industrial automation, perception and applied AI.

CSE (AI and Machine Learning)

AI and machine learning engineering, data science and applied AI.

BBA and MBA

Business analysis, supply chain, operations, marketing, sales and entrepreneurship.

Compare programmes

Our reporting pledge

The proposed annual reporting pledge is subject to agreement with programme leadership and the universities. The plan is to publish each measure separately.

Skills and projects

Show pass rates for each practical test, second attempts, and how many projects worked as specified.

Final-semester work

Show how many students worked with a company and how many worked in the Product Studio.

What graduates go on to do

Report job offers by role, higher studies and student-founded companies as distinct outcomes.

Employer feedback

Collect feedback about graduates after 3, 6 and 12 months.

For those who want the detail

Until the first cohort has work to show, the programme uses faculty and engineering reference builds to demonstrate the kinds of work students take on. Ask which reference projects you can see during your visit.

Individual skill tests, standard test stations and common marking rubrics help make each result traceable to the work a student actually did.

Read how we assess work

Ask to see the work.

During a visit, ask which reference projects you can see and how students will document what they build.
